quest.title: Garden Memories
quest.description: Now that you've left the lab, you should inform Katheryne that the contamination issue has been resolved.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x225, Primogem x60, Mora x13925, Guide to Admonition x5, Adventurer's Experience x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Anyway, so the contaminated region turned out to be a Ley Line effluence deep in the forest. Things are already getting back to normal.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I see. Thank you for your hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Once the excess Ley Line energy dissipates from the air, we should be able to make an announcement for residents to resume their normal activities.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: This is the stipulated reward. Please accept it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After leaving the Adventurers' Guild, Paimon takes you to a quiet place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is Karkata... going to be sent back to the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's already damaged, but Paimon feels sad thinking about it getting disassembled.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Me too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Then how about we find Tighnari tomorrow and ask him to not do that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon really wants to go right now, but Tighnari said that we would "discuss matters tomorrow." We'll probably make him mad if we go now, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Probably.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright then! We'll find Tighnari tomorrow and tell him not to disassemble Karkata!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari—

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Shh, keep your voice down.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Lilac Daphne, a daphne of the genus Thymelaeaceae, has a strong anticonvulsant effect. It can also be made into an anesthetic powder...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Extrapolating from these two data sets, it would be particularly potent against piscine species... Hey, make sure you're getting all this down.

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Karkata!?

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kalu! Kalu!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I thought I told you all to keep your voices low. Plants aren't afraid of noise, but your shouting is making my ears ring.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You didn't disassemble Karkata?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Why would I do that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon thought you said, "According to the Akademiya's policies"...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: So that's why you two barged in like barbarians at this hour. Fine, I suppose I wasn't clear enough about this yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What I meant was, according to the Akademiya's policies, all products of research must be destroyed. That's why we can't let the Akademiya discover that place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the real reason you stayed back was to...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Anyway, the first thing I did was repair Karkata. During my time at the Akademiya, I took an elective course at the Spantamad. Who knew it would prove useful one day.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We then buried Abattouy together. After organizing the research materials, I kept some as a souvenir, most of it was burned to hide the evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm not with the Akademiya, so what do their policies have to do with me? On the other hand, I am the Forest Watcher of the Avidya Forest. I have a duty to protect all life in the forest.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: All life brought forth in this world has meaning, and Karkata is no exception. If it exists, then it shouldn't be carelessly abandoned or destroyed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's great!

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you just said "life form." You recognize Karkata as a true living being now?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The possibility exists is all. It's hard to explain Karkata's efforts to "repair" Abattouy.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Abattouy only left behind a small portion of his research. Who knows how many commands he installed.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Maybe a conflict between all those commands resulted in this sort of behavior.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: From a more rigorous perspective, it is impossible to conclude that Karkata is a real life form, but the possibility exists — I am willing to believe in that.

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: By the way, I'm not interested in continuing research on this subject. I'm just letting it hang out here because this place is relatively secluded.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But as things stand now, it wouldn't be a bad idea to make it my research assistant. At the very least, it can record my experiments.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kalu! Kalu!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #How are you feeling {NICKNAME}? Sleep well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should go find Tighnari... Um... How do you think we should ask him...?
